blockers: ARCH-P3-R1-B1: next_pending_index selects the first pending event without checking dependency readiness, so a blocked acquire and its dependent consumer can prevent a later independent release from running. Select the earliest dependency-ready pending event and add the blocked-acquire/dependent-consumer/independent-release regression.

ARCH-P3-R1-B2: checkpoint identity and restore invariants do not cover the complete resumable state, including event program, last-event time, resource kind/arbitration, exact event/state keys, waiter/state consistency, processed-count/trace consistency, terminal consistency and time monotonicity.
ARCH-P3-R1-B3: frozen limits are incomplete. max_wait_for_nodes is absent and deadlock DFS is recursive/unbounded; input event count and waiter-drain completion budget are not fully enforced.
findings: The 45-member outer ledger and 26-member nested run ledger verified exactly.
Exact rational clocks, forward CDC, seven-field ordering and REPLAY_VALIDATE boundaries are implemented.
Referenced Phase 4 resources and ROUND_ROBIN fail closed, but inert unsupported declarations should also be rejected or explicitly scoped.
Reverse acknowledgement, queue protocol and credit behavior remain outside the implemented bridge primitive.
claim_boundary: Only CPU replay-validation primitives are supported; a freeze-ready dependency-aware engine, complete checkpoint integrity and bounded deadlock execution are not yet proven.
authorized_next_stage: Create a fresh Phase 3 CPU-only amendment candidate and repeat the complete suite and three-role same-hash review.
